PRINCIPAL-adjective, most important; noun, a person who has authority
ex: The principal ingredient in chocolate chip cookies is chocolate
chips.
ex: The principal of the school does the announcements each
morning.
PRINCIPLE-a general or fundamental truth
ex: The study was based on the principle of gravity.

QUOTE-verb, to cite; ex: I would like to quote Dickens in my next paper.
QUOTATION-noun, the act of citing
ex: The book of famous quotations inspired us all.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

STATIONARY-standing still
ex: The accident was my fault because I ran into a stationary object.
STATIONERY-writing paper
ex: My mother bought me stationery that was on recycled paper.

SUPPOSED TO-correct form for "to be obligated to" or "presumed to"
NOT "suppose to"
SUPPOSE-to guess or make a conjecture
ex: Do you suppose we will get to the airport on time? When is our
plane supposed to arrive? We are supposed to check our bags
before we board, but I suppose we could do that at the curb and
save time.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

THAN-use with comparisons
ex: I would rather go out to eat than eat at the dining hall.
THEN-at that time, or next
ex: I studied for my exam for seven hours, and then I went to bed.

THEIR-possessive form of they
ex: Their house is at the end of the block.
THERE-indicates location (hint: think of "here and there")
ex: There goes my chance of winning the lottery!
THEY'RE-contraction for "they are"
ex: They're in Europe for the summer--again!

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

THROUGH-by means of; finished; into or out of
ex: He plowed right through the other team's defensive line.
THREW-past tense of throw
ex: She threw away his love love letters.

THOROUGH-careful or complete
ex: John thoroughly cleaned his room; there was not even a speck of
dust when he finished.
THOUGH-however; nevertheless
ex: He's really a sweetheart though he looks tough on the outside.
THRU-abbreviated slang for through; not appropriate in standard writing
ex: We're thru for the day!

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

TO-toward
ex: I went to the University of Richmond.
TOO-also, or excessively
ex: He drank too many screwdrivers and was unable to drive home.
TWO-a number
ex: Only two students did not turn in the assignment.

WHO-pronoun, referring to a person or persons
ex: Jane wondered how Jack, who is so smart, could be having
difficulties in Calculus.
WHICH-pronoun, replacing a singular or plural thing(s); not used to refer
to persons
ex: Which section of history did you get into?
THAT-used to refer to things or a group or class of people
ex: I lost the book that I bought last week.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WHO-used as a subject or as a subject complement (see above)
ex: John is the man who can get the job done.
WHOM-used as an object
ex: Whom did Sarah choose as her replacement?

NOUNS
• Proper - particular person, place, thing
• Common - nouns in general sense
• Concrete - perceived by physical senses
• Abstract - not perceived; quality
• Count - can be counted
• Mass - non-countable; no plural form
• Collective - groups of persons, places, things
• Possessive - show ownership; with ’s

PRONOUNS

• Personal
• Possessive
• Reflexive/intensive

Maria hurt herself.
(reflexive)
Maria herself was hurt. (intensive)

• Relative

who, whom - people
which - animals, things
that - animals, things; persons as a group or anonymous

• Demonstrative

this, these, that, those

• Indefinite

all, another, both, each, either, few, most, nobody, several,
some, such, one, no one, everyone…

• Add information to another element in a sentence by

- large round wooden table

VERBS
• (Simple) PRESENT - basic form, simple form

- events exist always, usually, habitually
- present actions, state of being: I hear you.
- general truths: Leaves fall in autumn.
- scientific truths: The earth rotates on its axis.
- non-action; habitual action: I like music.
I run on Wednesdays and Sundays.
- schedules:The plane arrives at 2 o’clock.

• (Simple) PAST

- completed action: Jack planted the beanstalk.
- “d”, “-ed” or change “y” to “I” +” - ed

- completed condition: It rained last night.

Philippines.

• FUTURE

- activity that will or won’t exist in the future
- will/shall + base form of verb
- am/is/are + going to + infinitive
- am/is/are + -- ing form
- present form of verb (for schedules)
Angela will save fifty pesos.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

• PRESENT PERFECT

- has/have + Verb -en
- happened before (now) at an unspecified time in
the past
- Used adverbs with ever, never, already, yet, still,
just, for, since
I have been here since 7 o’clock.
- began in past & still continuing: for events
occurring at an indefinite time
They have had breakfast.
They had breakfast at 7 am.
(simple past if with time marker)

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

• PRESENT PERFECT

- habitual or continued action

- with events occurring at an indefinite or
unspecified time in the past (with ever, never,
before) Have you ever been to the USA before?

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

• PAST PERFECT
- had + Verb -en (past participle)

- describes past event completed before another event

When I arrived home, he had already left.
- in reported speech

- two past actions, one happened earlier
By the time the Senator finished his speech, the
audience had lost interest.

at the end of this month.

- am/is/are + Verb -ing
- action still in progress at present time
Angelito is still studying.

• PAST PROGRESSIVE

- was/were + Verb - ing
- past action began before and was in
progress at a particular time in the past.
They were climbing for twenty-seven days.

• FUTURE PROGRESSIVE

- will/shall + be + Verb -ing
- action will begin before another action

- has/have + been + Verb -ing
- began in the past, has continued into the
present, and may continue into the future

Jun has been working for four hours, and he hasn’t finished yet.

• PAST PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

- had + been + Verb -ing
- began in the past before another activity or time
in the past

Bert had been lecturing for 15 minutes before Joel arrived.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

• FUTURE PERFECT PROGRESSIVE

- will have + been + Verb -ing
- event is in progress before another event in the
future and will last for a particular time
Albert will have been lecturing for 15 minutes by the
time Joel arrives.

• Transitive

VERBS

- have an object (noun or pronoun) that completes
the action by showing who or what is affected by
action

• Intransitive

- express action without an object
The people laughed.

• Linking or auxiliary

- links to the subject a noun, pronoun or adjective that
describes it (subject complement)
- am, is, are, was, were, be, appear, grow, seem, stay,
become, look, smell, taste, feel, remain

PHRASAL VERBS
VERB + adverb or preposition

• creates a new meaning; alters usual meaning of the verb

Forms:

1. Verb + particle (no object)
break out

give in

go away grow up

War broke out in September.

2. Verb + particle + object
fall for

look after take after

She looked after her invalid mother.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

3. Verb + object + participle
answer back call back count in
I answered him back and took my chances.
4. Verb + particle + preposition with object
catch up with
look forward to
play around with
run away with
stick up for
walk out on

http://www.usingenglish.com/reference/phrasal-verbs/

MODAL VERBS
• can, could, may, might, ought, shall, should,
will, would
• Always the first word in a verb group
• All modals except “ought” are followed by the
base form of the verb
• Have only one form

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

USES of MODALS
Possibility
Can - something is possible

Probability and uncertainty
Could, might, may - indicates that you are not certain
whether something is possible but you think it is
Must, ought, should, will - express probability or
certainty

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Ability

Can - to talk about ability in the present and the
future
Could - talk about ability in the past
Be able to - talk about ability in the
present, past and future

Permission

Can and “be allowed to” - to talk about whether
someone has permission to do something or not
Can - to give someone permission to do something
Can or could - to ask for permission to do something

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Instructions and requests

Could you - to tell someone to do something politely; ask
for help

Suggestions

Could, couldn’t, shall - to make a suggestion
Shall we - to suggest doing something with someone
You might like or you might want - to make polite
suggestions
May as well or might as well - to suggest a sensible action
What about, Let’s, Why not, Why don’t

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Offers and invitations
Would you like - to offer something to someone or to
invite to do something
Can I, Could I, Shall I - offer to help someone

Wants and wishes
Would like - to say what you want
Would rather, would sooner, wouldn’t mind - to say
what you prefer

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Obligation and necessity

Have to, must, must have - to talk about obligation and
necessity in the present and future
Had to - to talk about obligation and necessity in the past
Need to - to talk about necessity
Don’t have to, don’t need to - it is not necessary to do
something

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PREPOSITIONS
• Links or shows relationship of nouns, pronouns and
phrases to other words in the sentence
• Occurs at the beginning of a phrase and always has an
object
Jose is married to Maria.

Commonly used prepositions:
about, above, across, after, against, along, amid, among, around, at,
before, behind, below, beneath, beside, beside, between, beyond,
but, by, concerning, down, except, for, in, into, of, off, into, under,
until, unto, up, upon, with, without  proper usage

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PREPOSITIONS: at, in, on
Use at to talk about a place as a point.

MORPOLOHIYA
• Ang morpolohiya ay pag-aaral ng mga morpema ng
isang wika.

• Ito ay sistema ng pagsasama-sama ng mga morpema sa
pagbuo ng mga salitang isang wika.
• Ang morpolohiya ay tumatalakay sa mga proseso at
mga alituntunin sa pagbubuo ng mga salita sa isang
wika.

MORPEMA
Ang morpema ang pinakamaliit na bahagi ng wika na
nagtataglay ng sariling kahulugan.
Hindi ito dapat ipagkamali sa pantig na likha ng mga
salita kung isinusulat o ang bawat saltik ng dila kapag
binibigkas.
Maraming mga pantig ang walang kahulugan sa sarili
kaya hindi maaaring tawaging morpema.

24

MORPEMA
Ang morpema ay maaaring isang salita o bahagi
lamang ng isang salita.
Ang mga pantig ay maaring pagsamasamahin upang
makabuo ng mga morpema.
Ang morpema ay ang isang kombinasyon ng ponema
na may kahulogan.

TAYUTAY

TAYUTAY
Ang tayutay ay salita o isang pahayag na
ginagamit upang bigyan diin ang isang kaisipan o
damdamin.
Sinasadya ng pagpapayahag na gumagamit ng
talinghaga o di-karaniwang salita o paraan ng
pagpapahayag upang bigyan diin ang kanyang
saloobin.

3
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

1. SIMILI O PAGTUTULAD
Di tiyak na paghahambing ng dalawang
magkaibang bagay. Ginagamitan ito ng mga
salitang: tulad ng, paris ng, kawangis ng, tila,
sing-, sim-, magkasing-, magkasim-, at iba pa. Ito
ay tinatawag na Simile sa Ingles.

Ang kaniyang kutis ay mamula-mula katulad ng
rosas.
4
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

2. METAPORA O PAGWAWANGIS
Tiyak na paghahambing ngunit hindi na
ginagamitan ng pangatnig. Nagpapahayag ito ng
paghahambing na nakalapat sa mga pangalan,
gawain, tawag o katangian ng bagay na
inihahambing.
Ikaw ay tinik sa aking lalamunan.

5
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

3. PERSONIPIKASYON O PAGTATAO
Ginagamit ito upang bigyang-buhay, pagtaglayin ng
mga katangiang pantao-talino, gawi, kilos ang mga
bagay na walang buhay sa pamamagitan ng mga
pananalitang nagsasaad ng kilos tulad ng pandiwa
at pangngalang-diwa.

Nagalak ang buwan sa kasiyahan ng mga tao sa
lupa.
6
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

4. PAGMAMALABIS O HAYPERBOLE
Ito ay lagpa-lagpasang pagpapasidhi ng kalabisan o
kakulangan ng isang tao, bagay, pangyayari,
kaisipan, damdamin at iba pang katangian,
kalagayan o katayuan.
Nabali ang tadyang ng malikot na langgam.
Lumindol sa bigat ng lakad niya.
7
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

5. SENEKDOKE O
PAGPAPALIT-SAKLAW
Isang bagay, konsepto kaisipan, isang bahagi ng
kabuuan ang binabanggit.
Ang masang Pilipino ay umaasa pa rin kay G.
Estrada.

8
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

6. PAG-UYAM
Isang uri ng ironya na ipinapahiwatig ang nais
iparating sa huli. Madalas itong nakakasakit ng
damdamin.
Tunay na napakahusay niyang magluto, kahit isa
ay walang kumain sa kaniyang karinderya.

9

7. PAGPAPALIT-TAWAG O METONIMYA
Pagpapalit ng katawagan o ngalan ng bagay na
tinutukoy.
Higit na makapangyarihan ang pluma kaysa espada.
Siya ang hudas ng kanilang samahan.

10
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

8. APOSTROPE O PAGTAWAG
Isang panawagan o pakiusap sa paraang tila
nakikipagusap sa isang tao o bagay.
O tukso, layuan mo ako.

11
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

9. PAG-UULIT
Aliterasyon - Ang unang titik o unang pantig ay
pare-pareho.
Anapora - Pag-uulit ng isang salitang nasa unahan
ng isang pahayag o ng isang sugnay.

Anadiplosis - Paggamit ng salita sa unahan at sa
hulihan ng pahayag o sugnay.

12
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

9. PAG-UULIT
Epipora - Pag-uulit naman ito ng isang salita sa
hulihan ng sunud-sunod na taludtod.

Empanodos o Pabalik na Pag-uulit - Pag-uulit
nang pagbaliktad ng mga pahayag.
Katapora - Paggamit ng isang salita na kadalasang
panghalip na tumutukoy sa isang salita o parirala
na binanggit sa hulihan
13
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

10. PAGTANGGI O LITOTES
Gumagamit ng katagang "hindi" na nagbabadya ng
pagsalungat o di-pagsang-ayon. Ito'y may himig
na pagkukunwari, isang kabaligtaran ng ibig
sabihin.
Hindi naman sa pagyayabang pero kaya ko ring
gawin ang ginagawa niya.

14
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

11. TANONG RETORIKAL
Tanong na ang layunin ay bigyang-diin ang isang uri
ng damdamin, at di nangangailangan ng
kasagutan.

Pag-ibig! Bakit kay lupit mo!
Katarungan? Katarungan bang matatawag ang
sinapit ko?
15
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

12. OKSIMORON
Pagtatambal ng dalawang salitang magkasalungat
na katanggap-tanggap.
Nakabibinging katahimikan ang sumalubong sa
kanyan pagbungad niya sa pintuan.

16

Philippines.

13. PAGTATAMBIS O ANTITHESIS
Nagpapahayag ng magkasalungat na bagay o ideya.

Mahirap maging kaibigan ang babaing iyan,
naiinis sa maganda at sa pangit, naiinggit sa
mayaman at nayayamot sa mahirap.

17

14. PAGLILIPAT-WIKA
Tulad ng pagbibigay-katauhan na pinasasabagay
ang mga katangiang pantao, na ginagamit ang
pang-uri.

18

15. PASUKDOL
Pataas na paghahanay ng mga salita o kaisipan
ayon sa kahalagahan nito mula sa pinakamababa
patungo sa pinakamataas na antas.

19
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

16. PANGHIHIMIG O ONOMATOPEYA
Ang paggamit ng mga salitang kung ano ang tunog
ay siyang kahulugan o ang pagkakahawig ng tunog
ng salita at ng diwa nito.
Dalawa ang uri nito:
a. Tuwirang onomatopeya
Ikaw’y iniluwal ng baha sa bundok
Hahala-halakhak at susutsut-sutsot.
- D. T. Mamaril, Ang Agos

16. PANGHIHIMIG O ONOMATOPEYA
b. Pahiwatig na onomatopeya
Ang suot ay puti’y may apoy sa bibig
Sa buong magdamag ay di matahimik,
Ngunit ang hiwagang di-sukat malirip
Kung bakit sa gabi lamang mamamasaid;
Kung araw, ang tao, kahit magsaliksik
Ang matandang ito’y hindi raw masilip,
Ngunit pagdilim na’t ang gabi’y masungit
Ano’t ang simbahan ay lumalangitngit?

Ang pangitain ay mga larawan, imahen, o palatandaang

Aking natatanaw si laurang sinta ko!
- F. Balagtas, Florante at Laura

18. TAGURI
Ang taguri ay patalinghagang pagtukoy sa isang tao upang

Bulaklak po ito ng lupang Tagalog
Kapatak ng luhang pangala’y kampupot.
- Jose C. de Jesus, “Bulaklak ng Lahing Kalinis-linisan”

MGA SAWIKAIN AT SALAWIKAIN

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

MGA SAWIKAIN AT SALAWIKAIN
Ang mga salawikain, kawikaan, kasabihan,
wikain, o sawikain ay mga maiiksing
pangungusap na lubhang makahulugan at
naglalayong magbigay patnubay sa ating pangaraw-araw na pamumuhay.

Naglalaman ito ng mga karunungan.

SAWIKAIN

ng tumpak na kahulugan ang mga kanyakanyang salita na nabuo.
Ito ay di-tuwirang pagbibigay kahulugan at
pagpapakita ng kaisipan at kaugalian ng isang
lugar.

SALAWIKAIN
Ang mga salawikaing Pilipino ay mga tradisyonal
na kasabihang ginagamit ng mga Pilipino batay
sa katutubong kalinangan, karunungan, at
pilosopiya mula sa buhay sa Pilipinas.

Kapag ginamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap,
gumaganap ang mga salawikain bilang mga
pagbibigay diin sa isang punto o isang kaisipan
ng paliwanag o dahilan: ang Pilosopiyang
Pilipino.
29
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

KAURIAN NG MGA SALAWIKAIN
1. Ang mga salawikaing etikal (yung mga
nagsasaad ng isang pangkalahatang gawi hinggil
sa buhay at sa mga batas na nangangasiwa sa
mismong pamumuhay)
2. Ang mga salawikaing nagmumungkahi ng mga
pagpapahalaga at nagtatakwil sa mga bisyo

3. Ang mga salawikaing nagpapadama ng isang
sistema ng mga pagpapahalaga
30

KAURIAN NG MGA SALAWIKAIN
4. Ang mga salawikaing naglalahad ng mga
pangkalahatang katotohanan at mga
pagmamasid tungkol sa buhay at kalikasan ng
tao

5. Ang mga salawikaing nakakatawa

31
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

MGA HALIMBAWA NG SALAWIKAIN
Pagkahaba-haba man ng prusisyon, sa
simbahan din ang tuloy.
Kahulugan: Sa tinagal-tagal man ng samahan ng
magkasintahan, sa bandang huli ay
humahantong din ito sa kasalan.

32
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

MGA HALIMBAWA NG SALAWIKAIN
Ang taong nagigipit, sa patalim man ay
kumakapit.
Kahulugan: Ang taong nagigipit kung minsan ay
napipilitang gumawa ng mapangahas na bagay na
maaaring maging dahilan upang lalu lamang siyang
magipit. Halimbawa, ang taong may mabigat na
pangangailangan ng pera ay nagagawang mangutang
ng patubuan, tulad ng five-six, na nagiging dahilan
upang lalu pa siyang mangailangan ng pera.

Pag makitid ang kumot,
magtiis kang mamaluktot.
Kahulugan: Kung nakakaranas ng kakulangan sa
buhay ang isang tao ay dapat siyang mamuhay
ng naaayon sa kanyang kakayahan. Matutong
magtipid at maging payak sa pamumuhay.

34

Kung hindi ukol, hindi bubukol.

asahang makakamtan kung hindi nakalaan para
sa iyo.

Nasa tao ang gawa nasa Diyos ang awa.

biyaya.

na nakalalason o nakasisira sa samahan ng

MGA HALIMBAWA NG SALAWIKAIN
Magkulang ka na sa magulang
huwag lamang sa iyong biyenan.
Kahulugan: Kadalasang ipinapayo eto sa mga
nagbabalak magpakasal o sa mga bagong mag-asawa
upang mapabuti ang kanilang pagsasama. Ang mga
magulang kase ay higit na mapagtatakpan o

MGA HALIMBAWA NG SALAWIKAIN
Kung ano ang puno, siya ang bunga.
Kahulugan: Ginagamit sa paghahambing ng anak sa
kanyang mga magulang. Sapagkat ang mga magulang
ang humuhubog sa pagkatao at pag-uugali ng anak,
ang anak ang nagiging larawan ng pagkatao at paguugali ng kanyang mga magulang. Ang mabuti (o
masamang) anak, ay karaniwang ibinubunga ng mabuti
(o masamang) mga magulang.

Halimbawa kung naging matulungin ka sa
kapwa ay tutulungan ka rin.

PANITIKANG FILIPINO
SA IBA’T IBANG PANAHON

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG KATUTUBO
 Bago pa dumating ang mga Kastila sa Pilipinas, mayroon
nang sining at panitikan ang mga sinaunang Pilipino.
 Karamihan sa mga panitikan nila’y yaong mga pasalindila gaya ng mga bulong, tugmang-bayan, bugtong,
epiko, salawikain at awiting-bayan na anyong patula;
mga kwentong-bayan, alamat at mito na anyong
tuluyan at ang mga katutubong sayaw at ritwal ng
babaylan bilang pinakaunang anyo ng dula sa bansa.
 Karamihan sa mga panitikang ito ay pasalin-dila.
42
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG KASTILA
 Dumating ang mga Kastila sa bansa taglay ang tatlong
Gs - GOD, GOLD at GLORY.
 Dumating sila na ang pangunahing layunin ay ihasik ang
Kristiyanismo, maghanap ng ginto at upang lalong
mapabantog sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng
kanilang nasasakop.

 Mahahati ang panitikan sa dalawa sa panahong ito: una
ay pamaksang pananampalataya at kabutihang-asal at
ang ikalawa ay ang panitikang panrebolusyon.
43
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG AMERIKANO
 Kung relihiyon ang naging pamana ng mga Kastila sa
Pilipino, edukasyon naman ang naging pangunahing
ipinamana ng mga Amerikano.

 Sa panahong ding ito isinilang ang mga ilang imortal na
makatang Pilipino na nagsisulat sa Ingles at Tagalog.
 Sa mga unang taon ng pananakop ng Amerikano sa
bansa, sumulat ang mga Pilipino sa Kastila, Tagalog at
iba pang wikang panlalawigan.
 Nagsimula umusbong ang mga panitikan sa Ingles
noong 1910 dahil sa mga bagong silang na manunulat.
44
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG AMERIKANO
 Kabilang sa mga manunulat sa panahong ito sina Cecilio

Apostol na sumulat ng mga oda para kay Rizal.
 Claro M. Recto - naging tanyag sa kanyang natatanging

mga talumpati.
 Lope K. Santos - sumulat ng obra-maestrang “Banaag

at Sikat” at nagpauso ng panitikang sosyalista.
 Jose Corazon de Jesus - tinaguriang Makata ng Pag-

ibig at may panulat-sagisag na “Huseng Batute”.
45
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG AMERIKANO
 Jose dela Cruz - may panulat-sagisag na ‘Huseng Sisiw’

dahil sisiw ang ipinababayad kapag nagpapagawa sa
kanya ng tulang pag-ibig.
 Severino Reyes - sumulat ng imortal na dulang

“Walang Sugat” at tinaguriang Ama ng Dulang Tagalog.
 Zoilo Galang - pinakaunang nobelistang (A Child of

Sorrow) Pilipino sa Ingles at maraming-marami pang
iba.
46
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PANAHON NG AMERIKANO
 Ang mga Amerikano ang nagpakilala ng mga fairy tale

sa mga Pilipino na ginamit ng mga gurong Tomasites sa
pagtuturo. Ipinakilala rin ng mga ito ang iba pang uri
(genre) ng panitikan gaya ng oda at nagpakilala sa
pinilakang-tabing - ang pelikula.
 Dula ang naging pangunahing panitikan sa panahong

ito. Dala nila ang mga bodabil na isang uri ng dula kung
saan umaawit at sumasayaw ang mga artista na
nagbunga sa sarsuwela ng Pilipinas.

 Sa panahon ding ito kinilala ang mga manunulat na

PANAHON NG PAGKAMIT NG KALAYAAN
HANGGANG KASALUKUYAN

iba’t ibang uri sa panahong ito ay ang pagkakalimbag ng

GENERAL EDUCATION

FILIPINO

Wikang Filipino
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

WIKANG FILIPINO

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

ANO ANG WIKANG FILIPINO?
Isinasaad ng Resolusyon Blg. 92-1 (Mayo 13, 1992) ng
Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino na ang Wikang Filipino ay
“Ang katutubong wika, pasalita at pasulat, sa Metro Manila, ang
Pambansang Punong Rehiyon, at sa iba pang sentrong urban sa
arkipelago, na ginagamit bilang wika ng komunikasyon ng mga
etnikong grupo. Tulad ng alinmang wikang buhay, ang Filipino ay
dumaraan sa proseso ng paglinang sa pamamagitan ng mga
panghihiram sa mga wika ng Pilipinas at, mga di-katutubong
wika sa ebolusyon ng iba’t ibang baryedad ng wika para sa iba’t
ibang sitwasyong sosyal, sa mga nagsasalita nito mula sa iba’t
ibang sanligang sosyal at para sa mga paksa ng talakayan at
matalisik na pagpapahayag.”
3
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Bago ito tinawag na Filipino, anu-ano ang mga
katawagan o pariralang ginamit sa pagtukoy sa
wikang pambansa?
Ang unang pariralang ginamit sa pagtukoy sa
wikang pambansa ay “pambansang wika ng
Pilipinas na batay sa Tagalog” sa bisa ng Kautusang
Tagapagpaganap Blg. 134 na nilagdaan ni
Pangulong Manuel L. Quezon noong Disyembre 30,
1937, alinsunod sa rekomendasyon ng unang Lupon
ng Surian ng Wikang Pambansa batay sa mga
resulta ng mga pag-aaral na itinakda ng Batas
Komonwelt Blg. 184, s. 1936.
4
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Bago ito tinawag na Filipino, anu-ano ang mga
katawagan o pariralang ginamit sa pagtukoy sa
wikang pambansa?
Pagkaraan ng 20 taon ng paggamit at pagtuturo ng
wikang pambansa, nilagdaan ni Kalihim Jose E.
Romero ng Edukasyon at Kultura ang
Memorandum Pangkagawaran Blg. 7 noong Agosto
13, 1959 na nag-aatas sa paggamit ng katawagan
“Pilipino” sa pagtukoy sa wikang pambansa upang
maikintal sa wikang pambansa ang di mapapawing
katangian ng ating pagkabansa.
5
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Bago ito tinawag na Filipino, anu-ano ang mga
katawagan o pariralang ginamit sa pagtukoy sa
wikang pambansa?
“At ang Konstitusyon ng 1937 ay nagtatadhana na
dapat magsagawa ng mga hakbang ang Batasang
Pambansa tungo sa paglinang at pormal na
pagpapatibay ng isang panlahat na wikang
pambansa na tatawaging `Filipino’. At hangga’t
walang ibang itinatadhana ang batas, ang Ingles at
Pilipino ang magiging mga wikang opsiyal.”

6
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Paano naging wikang opisyal ang Wikang
Pambansa?
 Sa bisa ng Batas Komonwelt Blg. 570 (Hulyo 7, 1940)
ang wikang pambansa ay ipinahayag bilang wikang
opisyal simula Hulyo 4, 1946.
 Ang atas na iyon ay inulit sa Konstitusyon ng 1973 na
nagsasaad na “Hangga’t walang ibang itinatadhana
ang batas, ang Ingles at Pilipino ang magiging
opisyal na mga wika.”
7
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

1. INTELEKTWALISASYON
 Proseso upang ang isang wikang di pa intelektwalisado

ay maitaas at mailagay sa antas na intelektwalisado.

 Layuning maging mabisang magamit sa mga

sopistikadong lawak ng karunungan.

 Sa kalahatan, mabisa ang wikang intelektwalisado hindi

lamang bilang wika ng tahanan, ng lansangan, ng
malikhaing panitikan, kundi bilang pang-agham, pangteknolohiya, at ng iba pang teknikal at mataas na antas
ng karunungan.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

2. MODERNISASYON
 Naglulunsad sa proseso ng pagsasanayang-bago

ng wika samantalang ang intelektwalisasyon ay
naglulunsad sa proseso ng pagtaas ng wika mula
sa mababang kalagayan nito.

 Kapag ang isang wika ay nagawang mabisang

magamit sa mataas na antas ng karunungan at
iba pang paksang teknikal, masasabing ito'y
modernisado na rin.
37
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

3. PURISMO
 Ang purismo ang ideyolohiya sa paggamit ng

tanging mga katutubong salita sa isang wika sa
layuning panatilihin itong dalisay mula sa mga
banyagaing salita.

 Ito ang ilan sa mga puristang salitang karamihan

ay ginawa noong 1960’s ng mga mag-aaral-wika.

 Ito ang panahon kung kailan naging pinakamainit

ang usaping purismo at pagpili ng pambansa
wika bukod pa sa Tagalog.

body:
Source: 14. MINDGYM_SOCIAL STUDIES-FALLACIES_LECTURE NOTES.pdf
Source type: pdf

FALLACIES
Social studies

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FALLACIES
1. Fallacies of Relevance
2. Fallacies of Presumption

3. Fallacies of Ambiguity

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FALLACIES OF RELEVANCE
1. ad baculum - Appeal to Force
2. ad misericordiam - Appeal to Pity
3. ad populum - Appeal to Emotion
4. ad verecundiam - Appeal to Authority
5. ad hominem - Mirror-image: appeal to authority

6. ad ignoratium - Appeal to Ignorance
7. ignoratio elenchi - Irrelevant Conclusion
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD BACULUM - APPEAL TO FORCE
In the appeal to force, someone in a position of power
threatens to bring down unfortunate consequences upon
anyone who dares to disagree with a proffered proposition.
Although it is rarely developed so explicitly, a fallacy of this
type might propose:
If you do not agree with my political opinions, you will receive a
grade of F for this course.
I believe that Herbert Hoover was the greatest President of the
United States.
Therefore, Herbert Hoover was the greatest President of the
United States.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD MISERICORDIAM - APPEAL TO PITY
Turning this on its head, an appeal to pity tries to win
acceptance by pointing out the unfortunate consequences
that will otherwise fall upon the speaker and others, for
whom we would then feel sorry.
I am a single parent, solely responsible for the financial
support of my children.
If you give me this traffic ticket, I will lose my license and be
unable to drive to work

If I cannot work, my children and I will become homeless and
may starve to death.
Therefore, you should not give me this traffic ticket.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD POPULUM - APPEAL TO EMOTION
In a more general fashion, the appeal to emotion
relies upon emotively charged language to arouse
strong feelings that may lead an audience to
accept its conclusion:
As all clear-thinking residents of our fine state have already
realized, the Governor's plan for financing public education
is nothing but the bloody-fanged wolf of socialism cleverly
disguised in the harmless sheep's clothing of concern for
children.
Therefore, the Governor's plan is bad public policy.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD VERECUNDIAM

APPEAL TO AUTHORITY
In an appeal to authority, the opinion of someone
famous or accomplished in another area of
expertise is supposed to guarantee the truth of a
conclusion. Thus, for example:
Federal Reserve Chair Alan Greenspan believes that
spiders are insects.

Therefore, spiders are insects.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD HOMINEM
The mirror-image of the appeal to authority is the ad hominem
argument, where we are encouraged to reject a proposition because it is
the stated opinion of someone regarded as disreputable in some way.
This can happen in several different ways, but all involve the claim that
the proposition must be false because of who believes it to be true:

Harold maintains that the legal age for drinking beer should
be 18 instead of 21.
But we all know that Harold . . .
. . . dresses funny and smells bad. or
. . . is 19 years old and would like to drink legally or
. . . believes that the legal age for voting should be 21, not 18 or
. . . doesn't understand the law any better than the rest of us.
Therefore, the legal age for drinking beer should be 21 instead of 18
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AD IGNORATIAM - APPEAL TO
IGNORANCE
An appeal to ignorance proposes that we accept
the truth of a proposition unless an opponent can
prove otherwise. Thus, for example:
No one has conclusively proven that there is no intelligent
life on the moons of Jupiter.
Therefore, there is intelligent life on the moons of Jupiter.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FALLACIES OF PRESUMPTION
1. Accident
2. Converse Accident
3. False Cause
4. Begging the Question
5. Complex Question

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

ACCIDENT
The fallacy of accident begins with the statement
of some principle that is true as a general rule, but
then errs by applying this principle to a specific
case that is unusual or atypical in some way.
Women earn less than men earn for doing thesame
work.
Oprah Winfrey is a woman.

Therefore, Oprah Winfrey earns less than male talkshow hosts.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

CONVERSE ACCIDENT
The fallacy of converse accident begins with a
specific case that is unusual or atypical in some
way, and then errs by deriving from this case the
truth of a general rule.
Dennis Rodman wears earrings and is an excellent
rebounder.
Therefore, people who wear earrings are excellent
rebounders.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FALSE CAUSE
The fallacy of false cause infers the presence of a
causal connection simply because events appear
to occur in correlation or (in the post hoc, ergo
propter hoc variety) temporal succession.
The moon was full on Thursday evening.
On Friday morning I overslept.
Therefore, the full moon caused me to oversleep.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

BEGGING THE QUESTION
Begging the question is the fallacy of using the
conclusion of an argument as one of the premises
offered in its own support. Although this often
happens in an implicit or disguised fashion, an
explicit version would look like this:
All dogs are mammals.
All mammals have hair.

Since animals with hair bear live young, dogs bear live young.
But all animals that bear live young are mammals.
Therefore, all dogs are mammals.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

COMPLEX QUESTION
The fallacy of complex question presupposes the
truth of its own conclusion by including it implicitly
in the statement of the issue to be considered:
Have you tried to stop watching too much television?

If so, then you admit that you do watch too much
television.
If not, then you must still be watching too much
television.
Therefore, you watch too much television.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FALLACIES OF AMBIGUITY
1. Ambiguous Langauge
2. Equivocation
3. Amphiboly

4. Accent
5. Composition
6. Division
7. Avoiding Fallacies

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AMBIGUOUS LANGUAGE
In addition to the fallacies of relevance and presumption
we examined in our previous lessons, there are several
patterns of incorrect reasoning that arise from the
imprecise use of language. An ambiguous word, phrase, or
sentence is one that has two or more distinct meanings.
The inferential relationship between the propositions
included in a single argument will be sure to hold only if
we are careful to employ exactly the same meaning in
each of them. The fallacies of ambiguity all involve a
confusion of two or more different senses.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

EQUIVOCATION
An equivocation trades upon the use of an
ambiguous word or phrase in one of its meanings in
one of the propositions of an argument but also in
another of its meanings in a second proposition.

Really exciting novels are rare.
But rare books are expensive.
Therefore, really exciting novels are expensive.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

AMPHIBOLY
An amphiboly can occur even when every term in
an argument is univocal, if the grammatical
construction of a sentence creates its own
ambiguity.

A reckless motorist Thursday struck and injured
a student who was jogging through the campus
in his pickup truck.
Therefore, it is unsafe to jog in your pickup truck.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

ACCENT
The fallacy of accent arises from an ambiguity
produced by a shift of spoken or written emphasis.

Jorge turned in his assignment on time today.
Therefore, Jorge usually turns in his assignments
late.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

COMPOSITION
The fallacy of composition involves an inference
from the attribution of some feature to every
individual member of a class (or part of a greater
whole) to the possession of the same feature by the
entire class (or whole).

Every course I took in college was wellorganized.

Therefore, my college education was wellorganized.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

DIVISION
Similarly, the fallacy of division involves an
inference from the attribution of some feature to an
entire class (or whole) to the possession of the same
feature by each of its individual members (or parts).

Ocelots are now dying out.
Sparky is an ocelot.
Therefore, Sparky is now dying out.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

General Education

SOCIAL STUDIES

Human Rights

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WHAT ARE HUMAN RIGHTS?
•

Human rights are the rights and freedoms that we
all have.

•

Some human rights are based on our physical
needs. The right to life. To food. To shelter.

•

Other human rights protect us. The right to be free
from torture, cruel treatment and abuse.

•

Human rights are also there to ensure we develop
to our fullest potential. The right to education. To
work. To participate in your community.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

HUMAN RIGHTS
• Human rights refer to the "basic rights and
freedoms to which all humans are entitled."
“All human beings are born free and equal in
dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason
and conscience and should act towards one
another in a spirit of brotherhood.”
-Article 1 of the United Nations Universal Declaration on Human Rights (UDHR)

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

INALIENABLE RIGHTS VS.
ALIENABLE RIGHTS
"Unalienable: incapable of being
alienated, that is, sold and transferred."

- Black's Law Dictionary, Sixth Edition, page 1523

•

Inalienable rights - Rights which are
not capable of being surrendered or
transferred without the consent of the
one possessing such rights (Morrison v. State,
Mo. App., 252 S.W.2d 97, 101.)‫‏‬

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

INALIENABLE RIGHTS
• Cannot be taken away from persons.
• Cannot be surrendered.
• An individual cannot give it up if s/he wishes to.

• An individual cannot exchange it with another
right.
• The government has the obligation to secure
them.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

NATURAL VS. LEGAL RIGHTS
•

Natural rights (also called moral rights or
inalienable rights) are rights which are not
contingent upon the laws, customs, or beliefs of a
particular society or polity.

•

Legal rights (sometimes also called civil rights or
statutory rights) are rights conveyed by a particular
polity, codified into legal statutes by some form of
legislature, and as such are contingent upon local
laws, customs, or beliefs.
Natural rights are thus necessarily universal, whereas legal rights are
culturally and politically relative.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PERFECT VS. IMPERFECT RIGHTS
•

Perfect rights - When the things which we have a right
to possess or the actions we have a right to do, or may
be fixed and determinate, the right is a perfect one
(enforceable by legal process).

•

Imperfect rights - When the thing or the actions are
vague and indeterminate, the right is an imperfect one
(not being enforceable titles).

•

Perfect rights are enforceable through court action but
imperfect rights are not.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PERFECT AND IMPERFECT RIGHTS
•

If a man demand his property, which is withheld
from him, the right that supports his demand is a
perfect one; because the thing demanded is fixed
and determinate.

•

But if a poor man ask relief from those from whom
he has reason to expect it, the right, which supports
his petition, is an imperfect one; because the relief
which he expects, is a vague indeterminate, thing.

•

The holder of a perfect right can ‘require’ the subject
under the related duty to perform that duty.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

ABSOLUTE, LIMITED, AND
QUALIFIED RIGHTS
•

Absolute rights - These rights cannot be limited in any way. They
can not be reduced or amended. Examples include the right to
protection from slavery or torture.

•

Limited Rights - These rights come with exceptions. An example is
the right to liberty, which can be lawfully restricted. Lawful arrest is
an example of a limited right.

•

Qualified Rights - Government interference with these rights is
allowed in special circumstances, and only when necessary in a
democratic society. The interference must fulfil a pressing social
need; pursue a legitimate aim; and be proportionate to the aims
being pursued. An example is government restrictions on the right to
assembly and association, in order to calm a riot.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

LAW VS. ETHICS
•

Ethics refers to motivation of human behavior which is
derived from internal conscience of human beings. In
general, ethics are the rules of right and wrong
behavior. The Merriam-Webster Collegiate Dictionary
defines ethics as "the principles of conduct governing
an individual or a group“.

•

Law deals with external and visible human behaviors.
Laws have penalties associated with them. If you don’t
obey the law, you are punished. Ethics, however, are
based on principles and values.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

RIGHTS & OBLIGATIONS

11
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

RIGHTS & OBLIGATIONS
ARE RELATED
• Every person has rights and obligations.
• The rights of persons are obligations for others.
• Every person is obliged to respect the rights of
others.
• Rights have limits.
• Every right has a corresponding duty.
• Rights and duties and related.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

HUMAN DIGNITY
13
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

HUMAN DIGNITY
• Intrinsic worth that inheres in every human being.

• From the Christian perspectives, the source of
human dignity is rooted in the concept of Christ’s
redemption and in our ultimate destiny of union

as the basis for rights and is neither granted by

human rights.

HUMAN RIGHTS

UNIVERSAL DECLARATION OF
HUMAN RIGHTS
HISTORICAL BACKGROUND
• On December 10, 1948 the General Assembly
of the United Nations adopted and proclaimed
the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

THE CONTENT OF THE UDHR
• Article 1 - "human beings are born free
and equal in dignity and rights..."
• Articles 2-21 - Civil and political rights
• Articles 22-29 - Economic and Social
Rights

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SIX CATEGORIES OF RIGHTS
IN THE UDHR
1. Security rights protect people against murder,
injury, and torture
2. Due process rights protect people against
arbitrary and excessively harsh punishments,
and require fair and public trials for those
accused of crimes.

3. Liberty rights protect people’s freedoms in
areas such as belief, expression, association,
and movement.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SIX CATEGORIES OF RIGHTS
IN THE UDHR
4. Political rights protect people’s liberty to
participate in politics by assembling,
protesting, voting, and serving in public office.
5. Equality rights guarantee equal citizenship,
equality before the law, and freedom from
discrimination.

6. Welfare rights require that people be provided
with education and protected against
starvation and severe poverty.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

FACTS ABOUT THE UDHR
 It is an international bill of rights. It covers all
of the standard rights, and adds welfare rights.
 It was conceived during World War II as a way
of creating a safer world and avoiding human
rights abuses.
 It helped give a fixed meaning to the idea of
human rights by providing an authoritative list.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

The United Nations
Universal Declaration
of Human Rights
(UDHR) is the most
famous human rights
agreement in the
world. It contains 30
human rights, as seen
on the right.
According to the
UDHR, you have the
right to…
22

CONVENTION ON THE RIGHTS
OF THE CHILD

23

WHO IS A CHILD?
A child is every human being below the age of 18
years unless, national laws recognize the age of
majority earlier .
-CRC, Article 1

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WHAT ARE THE RIGHTS OF
THE CHILD?
 To be born. To have a name and nationality.
 To be free. To have a family who will take care of me.
 To have a good education.
 To develop my potentials.
 To have enough food, shelter, a healthy and active
body.
 To be given the opportunity for play and leisure.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WHAT ARE THE RIGHTS OF
THE CHILD?
 To be given protection against abuse, danger and
violence brought by war and conflict.
 To be given the opportunity for play and leisure.
 To be given protection against abuse, danger and
violence brought by war and conflict.
 To live in a peaceful community.
 To be defended and assisted by the government.
 To be able to express own views.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Survival Rights
• Every child has the inherent right to life, and the
State has an obligation to ensure the child’s
survival and development.
• They include rights to adequate food, shelter,
clean water, and primary health care.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Development Rights
• These are rights to the resources, skills and
contributions necessary for the full
development of the child.
• They include rights to formal education, leisure
and recreation, cultural activities and
information.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Protection Rights
These rights include protection from all forms of
child abuse, neglect, exploitation and cruelty,
including the right to special protection in times of
war and protection from abuse in the criminal
justice system.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WRIT OF AMPARO
WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS
WRIT OF KALIKASAN

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS
The WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS, literally means "you have the
body," is defined as a writ or order directed to the person
detaining another, commanding him to produce the body of
the prisoner at a designated time and place, with the day and
cause of his caption and detention, to do, submit to, and
receive whatever the court or judge awarding the writ shall
consider in the behalf.
HABEAS CORPUS is a legal action, or writ, through which a
person can seek relief from the unlawful detention of him or
herself, or of another person. It protects the individual from
harming him or herself, or from being harmed by the judicial
system.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WRIT OF AMPARO
The petition for a writ of amparo is a remedy available to
any person whose right to life, liberty and security is
violated or threatened with violation by an unlawful act or
omission of a public official or employee, or of a private
individual or entity. The writ shall cover extralegal killings
and enforced disappearances or threats thereof.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WRIT OF HABEAS DATA
The writ of habeas data is a remedy available to any person
whose right to privacy in life, liberty or security is violated or
threatened by an unlawful act or omission of a public
official or employee, or of a private individual or entity
engaged in the gathering, collecting or storing of data or
information regarding the person, family, home and
correspondence of the aggrieved party.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

WRIT OF KALIKASAN
The Writ of Kalikasan will be the equivalent of the writ of
habeas corpus or of the writ of amparo in terms of
addressing ecological cases.
The Writ of Kalikasan and establishment of “green courts”
are pursuant to Article II, Section 16 of the Constitution,
which provides that “the State shall protect and advance
the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology
in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.”

General Education

SOCIAL STUDIES
Major Forms of
Government
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
1. Unitary System
•

A central government that holds all legitimate power.

•

There is little or no sphere of government autonomy to
local or component units like the provinces, barangays
and cities in the Philippines.

•

The central government is given all authority to make all
policies, although it may deputize other governmental
structures to act on its behalf.

•

Political power is more centralized (concentrated ore on
central authority) in unitary than federal systems.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
1. Unitary System
• Advantage - In this kind of government there is
clear hierarchical authority.
• Disadvantage - For the reason that the loyalty
of the citizens is focused on the governmental
authority, citizens tend to identify with the
country as a whole rather than with regional
authorities.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
2. Federal State
a. Local governmental authorities are set-up by the
constitution and these authorities are given certain
political decisions over which they have a legal
monopoly of control.
b. A federal government is one in which government
powers are divided between the central
government and its local government units as
specified in the constitution of the state.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
2. Federal State
c. In contrast to a unitary state, there is an explicit
sharing of power among levels of government
in a federation, and no level has legal power to
dominate any other level in policy domains.
d. The essence of federation is coordination not
hierarchy.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
2. Federal State
•

Advantage - Central or local government is
independent in its sphere of jurisdiction.

•

Disadvantage - There is a duplication of
offices and personnel in central and local
government, and to maintain this would be a
heavy financial burden to the government.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Systems of Government
3. Confederation
• This is an association wherein states delegate
certain power to a supranational central
government but retain primary power.
− Examples: United Nations, European Union,
ASEAN, APEC, United Arab Emirates

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Form of Distribution

Strengths

Weaknesses

• Clear authority
• Decisive control
• No stalemates
between center and
periphery

• Hyperconcentration of
power

of diversity and

• Duplication and
• Diversity represented
overlap of power

power
ultimate power

cooperation

compliance

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Key Terms
• DECENTRALIZATION - the transfer of powers from
central government to lower levels in a politicaladministrative and territorial hierarchy
• DEVOLUTION - the transfer of “natural resource
management to local individuals and institutions’
located within and outside of government”
• DECONCENTRATION - the process by which the
agents of central government control are relocated
and geographically dispersed

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of government

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
I. Ruled by One Person
A. MONARCHY
B. OLIGARCHY

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
A. MONARCHY
•

A government that has a single person who is generally
considered the ruler by the title and birthright. Titles
include: Czar, King, Queen, Emperor, Caesar, etc.

•

Power is absolute and is either taken through conquest
or passed down to family members without regard for
ability or appropriateness.

•

Society is formed around feudal groups or tribes in
which the ruling family delegates power and authority
based upon the desires of a single individual.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
A. MONARCHY
a. Absolute Monarchy - The monarch exercises absolute
power and wields executive, legislative and judicial
powers (predominated in France).
b. Limited Monarchy - The monarch delegates powers.
For example, the legislative body, judicial power by the
court and executive power by the King / Queen
exercise legislative power. They rule according to their
constitution. (United Kingdom, Belgium, the
Netherlands, Japan, Spain)
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
B. DICTATORSHIP
•

A type of government controlled by a single
individual and giving the people little or no individual
freedom.

•

Typically a person who rules by threat of force.

•

People who are loyal to a dictatorship swear
allegiance to the person first and the country second.

•

Fascism, Theocracies, Monarchies and
Communism can all be dictatorships.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
B. DICTATORSHIP
•

A Republic cannot be a dictatorship.

•

This can be applicable during a period of chaos or
discontent when the leader seeks emergency powers
to implement policies.

•

Can also be used by a leader to remain in office and
maintain power.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

title: LET General Education: MINDGYM SOCIAL STUDIES MAJOR FORMS OF GOVERNMENT LECTURE NOTES (Part 2)
body:
Source: 16. MINDGYM_SOCIAL STUDIES-MAJOR FORMS OF GOVERNMENT_LECTURE NOTES.pdf
Source type: pdf

Forms of Government
B. DICTATORSHIP
1. Authoritarianism - The political actions and decisions
of the ruler are not constrained, while political rights
and freedoms of the citizens are significantly limited.
2. Totalitarianism - Under this type of regime,
government uses ideology to captivate people’s
loyalty to the leader-dictator. The totalitarian dictator
wields absolute power. The use of coercion, violence
and force is a tool to maintain obedience from the
people.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
B. DICTATORSHIP
Characteristics of Totalitarianism
−

As a form of government the totalitarian dictatorship is built
on an ideological foundation. Government utilizes ideology to
captivate the people’s belief and loyalty to the leader-dictator.
A totalitarian leader wields absolute power.

−

The use of force, violent coercion and terrorism to control the
people.

−

Centralized control by the government of the nation’s
economy. Everyone must conform and accept the policies of
the dictatorship.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
B. DICTATORSHIP
Characteristics of Totalitarianism
−

To maximize the effectiveness of terror as a means of mass
control, the government controls all means of communication
and propaganda (eg. Soviet Union)

−

Totalitarianism is also centralized control by the government’s
economy. Every business enterprise is regulated, coordinated
by the existing regime.

−

Examples: Nazism - Adolf Hitler, Fascism - Benito Mussolini,
Chinese Communism - Mao Tze Tung

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
II. Ruled by the Few
A. ARISTOCRACY
Derived from the Greek etymology “Aristo” which
means the “best” and “Kratia or Kratos” which means
rule. A government by the “best members of the
community. Aristocrats are presumably men of the
highest intelligence and integrity. They belong to the
elite in society. Their social status, wealth and political
power are inherited.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
II. Ruled by the Few
B. OLIGARCHY
This is also a government of a wealthy few but they do
not come from nobility like aristocrats. Oligarchs
believe that the most important requisites to claim of
power are wealth, good social positions and education;
it is unlikely that oligarchy could serve the interest of
the masses since they use their positions in the
government for their personal benefit. They build
economic empires for themselves and their family.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
III. Ruled by Many
DEMOCRACY
“Demos” derived from the Greek term for people
and “kratos” which means rule. The Constitution
guarantees freedom of speech, freedom of
association, freedom of religion and freedom of
expression.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
III. Ruled by Many
Two essential features of Democracy:
1. Majority Rule - the majority of citizens choose their
leaders who then have the mandate to govern and
make public policies.
2. Minority Rights - This is ensured so long as the
minority of citizens openly attempts to win majority
support for leaders and policies without loss of
individual rights just as the majority enjoys these
rights.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
III. Ruled by Many
A democracy is made to work when the following interact:
1.

Citizens - Active participation of the citizenry is necessary in order to
prevent government from committing abuses. Citizens can help to balance
between power and authority of government officials. Citizens should
exercise their freedom and rights within the bounds of the Constitution
and the law, just as government should exercise its authority within limits.

2.

Suffrage and the Electoral Process - Suffrage is the right conferred by law
upon a qualified group of citizens to choose their public officials and to
participate in the determination of proposed policies whenever these
policies are submitted to them for approval. The citizens must use this right
to elect qualified people who can govern competently and responsibly.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Forms of Government
III. Ruled by Many
A democracy is made to work when the following interact:
3.

Political Parties - Intertwined with democratic government, this is a group
of officials or would-be officials who are linked with a sizable group of
citizens into an organization; a chief object of this organization is to ensure
that its officials attain power or are maintained in power. The party’s nature
as a structure, tying together a large group of officials and citizens, provides
an avenue by which one part may control or communicate with another. It
is this that has made it such a versatile tool of modern politics.

4.

Interest Groups - is an organized group of citizens one of whose goals is to
ensure that the state follows. They aim to represent public opinion and
having it heard in an organized and effective way to government
authorities.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Autocracy
• A single person holds power.
• Power is usually inherited or kept by force, i.e.
dictatorships and monarchies.
• Government by a single person having
unlimited power; despotism (domination
through threat of punishment and violence)

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Oligarchy
• A few individuals hold power.
• Wealth and military power usually influence
who the oligarchs will be.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Democracy
• Government is elected by the people.
• A democracy is determined either directly or
through elected representatives.

title: LET General Education: MINDGYM SOCIAL STUDIES MAJOR FORMS OF GOVERNMENT LECTURE NOTES (Part 3)
body:
Source: 16. MINDGYM_SOCIAL STUDIES-MAJOR FORMS OF GOVERNMENT_LECTURE NOTES.pdf
Source type: pdf

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Anarchy
• A situation where there is no government.
• This can happen after a civil war in a country,
when a government has been destroyed and
rival groups are fighting to take its place.
• Anarchists are people who believe that
government is a bad thing in that it stops
people organizing their own lives

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Capitalist
• In a capitalist or free-market country, people
can own their own businesses and property.
• People can also buy services for private use,
such as healthcare.
• But most capitalist governments also provide
their own education, health and welfare
services.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Communist
• In a communist country, the government owns
property such as businesses and farms.
• It provides its people's healthcare, education
and welfare.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Republic
• A republic is a country that has no monarch.
• The head of the country is usually an elected
president.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Revolutionary
• If a government is overthrown by force, the
new ruling group is sometimes called a
revolutionary government.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Presidential vs
Parliamentary

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Presidential System
• The executive power is exercised by a single
president elected by popular vote.
• S/he holds office for a specific period of time
fixed by the constitution of the state.
• S/he appoints the members of his / her
cabinet who are responsible to the president.
Their service is co-terminus with the
presidents.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Presidential System
• An essential element of this system is the
separation of powers of the executive,
legislative, and judicial branches, which is
made more effective by checks and balances
of the 3 branches.
• This is the form of government of the United
States and the Philippines.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Parliamentary System
•

Executive power belongs to the Prime Minister and his
Cabinet. They are the leaders of the majority party in
the Parliament and they remain in office as long as
they have the confidence and support of the
parliamentary majority.

•

They participate in parliamentary debates and defend
their policies and bills, and see to it that they are
approved for the nations welfare and for their
respective constituents, since they are also elected as
members of parliament.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Parliamentary System
• They are responsible to Parliament for their
acts and decisions as members of the Cabinet.
• The Prime Minister and his cabinet are
removable by Parliament by means of
parliamentary censure on the members of the
cabinet and a no-confidence vote against the
Prime Minister.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Parliamentary System
1. Collective ministerial responsibility
2. Fusion of executive and legislative power
3. Cabinet responsibility to parliament
4. Party discipline

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Presidential VS Parliamentary

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2011 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

title: LET General Education: MINDGYM SOCIAL STUDIES PHILIPPINE HISTORY LECTURE NOTES (Part 1)
body:
Source: 17. MINDGYM_SOCIAL STUDIES-PHILIPPINE HISTORY_LECTURE NOTES.pdf
Source type: pdf

PHILIPPINE HISTORY
TIMELINE

1
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

PHILIPPINE HISTORY
I.

PRE-HISTORIC TIMES

II. SPANISH COLONIZATION
III. BRITISH INVASION
IV. THE AMERICAN OCCUPATION

V. THE JAPANESE OCCUPATION

2
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

Spanish Colonization

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1521, Mar 16. A Spanish expedition, sailing across the
Pacific Ocean from east to west, and led by the
Portuguese Ferdinand Magellan (died Apr 27, 1521)
lands on Homonhon Island east of Samar with three
small ships, named the Concepcion, Trinidad and
Victoria. Magellan calls the place San Lazaro Island
since March 16 is Saint Lazarus day.

•

1521, Mar 31. The first mass on Philippine soil is
celebrated on Limasawa.

•

1521, Apr 27. Magellan dies in a battle with Lapu-Lapu,
chieftain of Mactan, an island near Cebu.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1543, Feb 2. The leader of the most successful Spanish
expedition after Magellan, Ruy Lopez de Villalobos
(died Apr 4, 1546) arrives in the archipelago. He names
the islands the Philippines in honor of the son of King
Charles I, Philip II (1556-1598) of Spain.

•

1565, Feb 13. With four ships and 380 men, Miguel
Lopez de Legaspi arrives in the Philippines.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
• 1589. The Spaniards establish the first school
in the Philippines, the College of San Ignacio.

• 1600. The Galleon trade between Manila and
Acapulco, Mexico begins. But Manila serves
merely as a transshipment port for the
exchange of goods between Spain and Mexico
on the one side and China on the other.
• 1603. Chinese insurrection in Manila.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1762, Sep 22. In a side encounter of the European
Seven Years War, the British attack Manila with 13
vessels and 6,830 men under the command of
General William Draper and Admiral Samuel Corning.
The British win the battle and occupy the city.

•

1812, Mar 19. The Spanish Cortes promulgates the
Cadiz Constitution. It is a liberal constitution, vesting
sovereignty in the people, recognizing the equality of
men and the individual liberty of the citizen, and
granting suffrage, but providing for a hereditary
monarchy and for Catholicism as the state religion.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1863. The educational system in the archipelago is
reformed, allowing the natives higher levels of training.
Wealthier native families start sending their children to
study in Spain.

•

1872, Feb 17. Three martyr priests are publicly
garroted as alleged leaders of the Cavite Conspiracy, a
movement for secularization and nationalism, which is
distasteful to the Spanish friars. They are Jose Burgos
(born Feb 9, 1837), Mariano Gomez (born Aug 2, 1799)
and Jacinto Zamora (born Aug 14, 1835).

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1882, Mar 3. A talented offspring of the native elite,
Jose Protacio Rizal Mercado y Alonso Realonda (Jun
19, 1861 - Dec 30, 1896) leaves Manila for Barcelona to
continue his studies in medicine.

•

1888, Dec 13. Filipinos in Barcelona establish the
organization La Solidaridad. It demands for the
Philippines freedom of press, speech and assembly,
equality before the law, participation in governmental
affairs, social and political freedom and representation
in the Spanish Cortes.

Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1892, Jul 3. In Ilaya St, Tondo, Rizal founds La Liga
Filipina to give the people a chance for direct
involvement in the reform movement. Andres
Bonifacio (Nov 30, 1863 - May 10, 1897) is one of
Rizal's partners.

•

1894, Jul 8. Andres Bonifacio forms the Katipunan. Its
members come from the lower and the middle class.
The organization wants to awaken nationalism and
free the Filipino people from Spanish oppression and
friar despotism. The organization believes that reforms
can only be obtained by means of a revolution.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1896, Aug 19. Spanish authorities discover the
Katipunan when one of its members, Teodoro Paterno,
betrays the organization to an Agustinian priest, Fr.
Mariano Gil. All those implicated are ordered arrested
but many Katipuneros evade arrest and flee to the hills
of Balintawak.

•

1896, Aug 23. A revolution is proclaimed by Bonifacio.
The event is marked in history as the Cry of
Balintawak. In this instance, Filipinos tear up their
cedulas (I.D. cards) issued by the Spanish government
and thereby mark the beginning of the uprising against
the Spaniards.
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1896, Oct 31. A new group of the Katipunan is formed
in Cavite; it discards the leadership of Andres Bonifacio
and is headed by Emilio Aguinaldo (Mar 22, 1869 - Feb
6, 1964).

•

1896, Nov 13. Rizal arrives in Manila and is immediately
imprisoned at Fort Santiago.

•

1896, Dec 20. Rizal is sentenced to death by a Spanish
court martial. Governor Camilo Polavieja orders his
execution.

•

1896, Dec 30. The Spaniards execute Jose Rizal in
Bagumbayan (today's Rizal Park).
Exclusively for My Review Coach online LET review. Not for redistribution. © 2014 My Review Coach of

Philippines.

SPANISH COLONIZATION
•

1897, Mar 22. The Katipunan holds its election.
Aguinaldo is elected as president while Bonifacio is
elected only as director of war. Bonifacio is insulted by
the election results and refuses to recognize the new
leadership.

•
